Description: In the early morning, Edmund Galley paces alone in the Living room and talks to himself, showing tension and a desire to control the situation. After hearing the familiar piano piece and Victoria Maseko’s shout, he quickly leaves the Living room.
Location: Living room（Living room）
Key Information:
  - In the early-morning time slot, Edmund Galley is alone in the Living room, pacing back and forth.
  - He gradually begins to hear sounds coming from other parts of the villa, indicating the house is becoming active again.
  - Edmund Galley mutters to himself, “He has to do what I say—I’ve got a gun,” implying he possesses a gun and intends to control someone with it.
  - After a brief silence, piano music starts in the Living room.
  - This piano piece is the same as the one played in the time-point 01 scene, forming an obvious repeating clue.
  - Then comes the sound of Victoria Maseko (No. 7) shouting.
  - Upon hearing the shout, Edmund Galley immediately leaves the Living room, clearly preparing to intervene in the sudden incident.
Characters:
  [Edmund Galley（Edmund Galley）] Person No. 6, the male head of the villa.
    · Paces alone in the Living room in the early morning and remains awake.
    · Explicitly says he has a gun, implying an intent to take control of the situation.
    · Leaves the Living room quickly after piano music and Victoria Maseko’s shout occur.
